description: Ritual sacrifice was an important feature of many ancient religions, serving to honor the gods, seek divine favor, fulfill vows, and strengthen communal bonds. Greeks and Romans commonly sacrificed animals, wine, grain, and incense at public altars; Carthaginians and other Phoenician peoples maintained elaborate temple offerings and sacrificial rites; Persians emphasized sacred fire, libations, and carefully prescribed offerings; while Egyptian, Indian, Celtic, Germanic, and other traditions developed their own forms of animal, food, drink, and votive sacrifice. These ceremonies were often conducted by priests or civic officials and accompanied festivals, military campaigns, treaties, funerals, and other major events where divine approval was considered essential.
